solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Obvious when persevering without hint of inconvenience

indicators.note: to go without something is to lack it, so that letter is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: someone persevering keeps at it patiently

indicators.note: a hint is only a small taste of something, so just the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of inconvenience

explanation.surface: Someone grimly sticking at a task makes it plain that nothing is bothering them.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PATIENT and drop its I to leave PATENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plainly evident, as in a patent lie or a patent absurdity.

clue.text: Nathaniel briefly turns to the church after depression caused by poor wage

indicators.note: said briefly, a name is cut down to its short pet form, which is then joined to the other parts

parts.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground

indicators.note: something that turns round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Nat is the short form of the name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A badly paid man called Nathaniel, low in spirits, seeks comfort in religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After depression' places the hollow first; 'briefly' shortens the name before it is turned round. CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small, inadequate amount of money paid for work.

clue.text: Right about a woman going over, seconds before closure of level crossing

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: RT is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written

indicators.note: something going over another covers it on both sides, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a woman's name
S is the abbreviation for seconds

indicators.note: the closure of a word is where it ends, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of level

explanation.surface: A woman dashes over a level crossing seconds before the barriers come down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level crossing' reads as one phrase, but 'level' only supplies its last letter and 'crossing' alone is the definition. VERA wraps round S.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is the act of passing across or over something, which is exactly what a crossing is.

clue.text: Announcer's familiar with narrow margin of victory

indicators.note: an announcer speaks words out loud, so what counts is the sound rather than the spelling

parts.note: to be familiar with something is to know it

explanation.surface: A racecourse commentator knows all about photo finishes and close winners.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is': the announcer's version of 'is familiar with' is how KNOWS is said.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, a horse that wins by a nose finishes only the length of its muzzle ahead, the smallest recorded winning distance.

clue.text: Learned of the French whip found in river on the way back

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so these letters go within another word
travelling back means going in the opposite direction, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
du is French for 'of the'
the cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip

explanation.surface: A scholar hears of a French whip being discovered in a river on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed river splits after its first letter to take the French and the whip. 'Learned' is said as two syllables here.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned describes someone with much knowledge from study, the same as well schooled.

clue.text: Popular book about head of ICE in Washington

indicators.note: being in a place means being surrounded by it, so these letters sit inside another piece

parts.note: DC, District of Columbia, is the city's abbreviation

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of ICE

explanation.surface: A bestselling book about the boss of the US immigration agency is out in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE here is US Immigration and Customs Enforcement; only its first letter is used. 'About' turns the book round before it goes inside Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of or for ordinary people, so popular in the sense of belonging to the common folk.

clue.text: Chilean cop's vehicle seen by graduate around one in front of coffee shop

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
the Roman numeral for one
Caffè Nero is a British chain of coffee shops

explanation.surface: A Chilean police car is spotted near a graduate standing outside a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' turns only the graduate's two letters, not the one that follows. Caffè Nero is a British coffee chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A carabinero is a member of the Carabineros de Chile, the country's national police force; the clue's possessive reads as 'is'.

clue.text: Cape Town's top dancing girl

indicators.note: the top of a word written downwards is its first letter, so only that is used

parts.note: the first letter of Town
an alma or almah is an Egyptian dancing girl

explanation.surface: Cape Town's star dancer is the best girl in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Town reads as the South African city, but 'Cape' is the definition, a garment, and 'Town' gives only its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A talma is a long nineteenth-century cloak or short cape, named after a French actor who wore one.

clue.text: Settle for some homemade cider

indicators.note: only some of the words is wanted, a run of letters taken from inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone happy to make do with a little home-brewed cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle for' looks like the phrase meaning accept, but 'for' just links: homeMADE CIDEr holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a question is to resolve it, to make up your mind about it.

clue.text: Appropriate for Yeats perhaps to embrace luck? Not half

indicators.note: saying not half removes half of the word, so only its other half remains
to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet; 'perhaps' marks him as one example
the second half of the word, its first half dropped

explanation.surface: Was it fitting for Yeats to trust to luck? Not half, comes the hearty answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' sounds like the British exclamation meaning 'very much so', but it strips LU from luck. 'Appropriate' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket something is to take it for yourself, often dishonestly, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: Convert managed to fill extremely tedious document

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so these letters sit within another pair
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of tedious
to run a business is to manage it
a form is an official document to fill in

explanation.surface: A convert to bureaucracy managed to fill in an utterly dull form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To fill' looks like filling in the form, but it puts the verb inside the ends of 'tedious'.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to change it into another form, the same as altering it completely.

clue.text: Roman Catholic priest breaking souvenir

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece splits the other

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest smashes a holy keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is the crossword's standard priest, from the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept as a memento of the past, a keepsake that recalls a person or event.

clue.text: Allege as a fact when edging away from partygoers

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outer letters, so taking those away leaves the inside

parts.note: ravers go to wild parties

explanation.surface: Someone states their case while sidling away from a crowd of revellers.
explanation.walkthrough: RAVERS loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or assert positively that something is true.

clue.text: Means of transport with broad seat designed to carry king

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so another letter goes in among these
something designed is newly arranged to a plan, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A royal carriage with a wide seat built to carry the king.
explanation.walkthrough: K joins the ten letters of 'broad seat' before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A skateboard is a board on wheels that a rider stands on to travel, so a way of getting about.

clue.text: Monitor the activities of son after quick look over bill

indicators.note: turned over, a word runs the other way, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look
a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent checks up on a son after glancing over his bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of son' looks like part of the definition, but 'of' ends the definition and 'son' is taken whole, placed last.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep tabs on someone is an idiom for watching closely what they are doing.

clue.text: What is suffered to obtain seating at the front that's most comfortable

indicators.note: to obtain is to get and hold, so one piece takes others inside it

parts.note: a cost is a loss or penalty suffered

indicators.note: the front of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of seating
i.e. (id est) means 'that is'

explanation.surface: The discomfort you put up with to grab the comfiest front seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' abbreviates 'that is', which crosswords render as the Latin abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy means snug and comfortable, so its superlative names the greatest comfort.

clue.text: Run together with Italian scoundrel

parts.note: con is Italian for 'with'
a cur is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Two people make off together with an Italian rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With Italian' reads as accompanying the Italian, but it asks for the Italian word for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Events concur when they happen at the same time, coinciding or running side by side.

clue.text: Merciless international organisation hits back in Gabon

parts.note: the United Nations

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks
taken as written
G is Gabon's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: A ruthless global body strikes back in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Gabon' looks like a location; IN is taken as written and G is the country's vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsparing means showing no leniency or mercy, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Endorse article after Henry died from a stroke

parts.note: to back a proposal is to endorse it
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an is the indefinite article
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A newspaper item reporting that a man called Henry died of a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After Henry' puts AN after H. 'Stroke' suggests illness, but it is a tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis and other racket games, a backhand is a shot played with the back of the hand facing the ball.

clue.text: Excellent debut of singer to delight in

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of singer
to lap up praise is to relish it

explanation.surface: A singer's brilliant first performance, a thing to enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap-up is British for lavish and splendid, usually of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, first-rate one, so slap-up is an informal term for splendid.

clue.text: Penny likely to be easily influenced

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
liable to do something means likely to

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny is probably a pushover.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name, but it is the coin, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliable means bendable, and figuratively a pliable person is readily persuaded or swayed.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval over soldiers returning with Afghan's original hot sauce

indicators.note: lying over something means covering it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: an audience hisses to show disapproval

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the RA is the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: what is original comes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Afghan

explanation.surface: Troops heading home from Afghanistan are greeted with jeers and a fiery condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery is the usual crossword source for soldiers; 'over' means the jeer encloses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a spicy North African chilli paste used as a hot condiment.

clue.text: Deal with bad weather reportedly around North Dakota

indicators.note: something placed around another surrounds it, so one piece sits inside
what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: hail is bad weather, said the same as hale
ND is the US state abbreviation

explanation.surface: Coping with storms said to be sweeping round a US prairie state.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is spelt as the word meaning healthy and vigorous, which then wraps the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a problem is to cope with it or manage it.

clue.text: Horse we bought at the start from fairy queen's retainer

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
taken as written

indicators.note: what comes at the start of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of bought

explanation.surface: We bought a horse from a fairy queen's servant.
explanation.walkthrough: The fairy queen is Titania in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobweb is one of the fairies who attend Titania in Shakespeare's play, serving the queen and Bottom.

clue.text: Companies providing musical dramas forced into cuts

indicators.note: a blade that cuts opens a gap, so one piece is slotted inside another

parts.note: operas are dramas set to music

indicators.note: something forced is pushed out of its natural shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Opera companies forced into making cuts to their musical productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' wants to be the definition, surgical operations; it is the instruction that INTO, rearranged, cuts into OPERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation can mean a business or organisation, so operations are firms or enterprises.

clue.text: Record producer's last to be gripped by reflective single

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run in reverse
something gripped is held tight inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: lone means single, solitary

indicators.note: the last of a word is where it finishes, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of producer

explanation.surface: A record producer's final release is a thoughtful single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' and 'single' look like music; 'Record' is the definition, a verb, and 'single' means lone.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to enter a name on an official list or register, which is to record it.

clue.text: Want chop left for husband

indicators.note: one letter is put for another, so the letter for left takes the place of the letter for husband

parts.note: to hack is to chop roughly
L is the abbreviation for left
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife wants a lamb chop left out for her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: HACK swaps its H for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means a shortage or absence, which is a lack of something.

clue.text: Withhold assent to examine duck

parts.note: to vet is to examine carefully
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Refusing to let a vet look over a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of zero, so it stands for the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a proposal is to reject it formally, refusing the approval it needs.

clue.text: Goes for frying pans stocked by Rackhams primarily

indicators.note: goods stocked in a shop are held within it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: woks are Chinese frying pans

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Rackhams

explanation.surface: A shopper picks the frying pans a department store mainly sells.
explanation.walkthrough: Rackhams was a department store in Birmingham. R sits inside WOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that goes is running properly, which is to say it works or functions.

clue.text: Elegance at the outset possessed by L Blair amazing North American dancer

indicators.note: what is possessed is held within, so one letter goes inside the others
something amazing leaves you all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Elegance
NA is the abbreviation for North American

explanation.surface: An amazingly graceful North American dancer whose name is L. Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: E joins L BLAIR and the seven letters are rearranged before NA is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer, especially one of high rank in a company.

clue.text: Weapon hidden in disagreeable stable

indicators.note: a thing concealed within another is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: bad can mean unpleasant or disagreeable
a lance is a long spear

explanation.surface: A weapon is concealed in an unpleasant horse stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden in' usually signals a run of letters inside the words, but no such run exists here; it puts the weapon inside. 'Stable' is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something balanced is steady and in equilibrium, not liable to tip over.

clue.text: Devised in order to acquire endless diamonds

indicators.note: without an end, a word loses its final letter

parts.note: for can mean with the aim of
get, minus its last letter
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A scheme dreamt up to get hold of an unlimited supply of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: GET loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge a plan or agreement is to create it through effort, so forged means devised or worked out.
